title: Investigation of Performance and Fuel Oil Corrosion Resistance of Semi-Flexible Pavement with Incorporation of Crushed Glass Waste
content: Semi-flexible pavement (SFP) is considered a viable, economic and alternative to conventional pavements. SFP has high strength properties and is constructed by pouring a high fluidity-workable cement grout (HFCG) onto the surface of an open-graded asphalt (OGA) structure layer. SFP damage caused by significant spillage of aggressive materials (i.e. fuel oil) requires huge amounts of money to be budgeted for the rehabilitation and maintenance, and this expenditure motivates to research for solutions to reduce the fuel oil cavitation damage generation and costs. One of eco-friendly solutions is the inclusion of glass waste (GW) into OGA mattress construction materials for SFP, reducing the depletion of natural resources and decreasing landfill solid wastes. The main objective of the research is to investigate the performance and fuel oil resistance of SFP composites containing various levels of glass aggregate (GlaSFlex composites). The fine glass aggregate (FGA) was replaced with fine virgin aggregate at levels of 0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% by mass. The results indicated the applicability of FGA for 100% replacement of fine aggregate in GlaSFlex composite, as it had high performance properties in terms of compressive strength, Marshall stability, resistance to fuel spillage, stiffness modulus and residual durability. Conclusively, GlaSFlex composite between 40% and 60% demonstrated superior performance properties compared to other composites.
